  "vulnerability_pattern": "TOCTOU on shared memory: values read from user-writable memory for validation are re-read for use, allowing validation bypass via concurrent modification.",
  "patch": "commit 22ba97ea9cc1f63a0d0244fae38057ed452b6ac7
Author: Jason Xing <kerneljasonxing@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat May 30 12:26:30 2026 +0800

    xsk: cache csum_start/csum_offset to fix TOCTOU in xsk_skb_metadata()
    
    The TX metadata area resides in the UMEM buffer which is memory-mapped
    and concurrently writable by userspace. In xsk_skb_metadata(),
    csum_start and csum_offset are read from shared memory for bounds
    validation, then read again for skb assignment. A malicious userspace
    application can race to overwrite these values between the two reads,
    bypassing the bounds check and causing out-of-bounds memory access
    during checksum computation in the transmit path.
    
    Fix this by reading csum_start and csum_offset into local variables
    once, then using the local copies for both validation and assignment.
    
    Note that other metadata fields (flags, launch_time) and the cached
    csum fields may be mutually inconsistent due to concurrent userspace
    writes, but this is benign: the only security-critical invariant is
    that each field's validated value is the same one used, which local
    caching guarantees.
    
    Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260503200927.73EA1C2BCB4@smtp.kernel.org/
    Reviewed-by: Maciej Fijalkowski <maciej.fijalkowski@intel.com>
    Signed-off-by: Jason Xing <kernelxing@tencent.com>
    Acked-by: Stanislav Fomichev <sdf@fomichev.me>

    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

content.thinking:
This is the classic pre-TX-metadata XSK code (before commit 48eb03dd2630 which added TX timestamp/checksum offload support). The snapshot s04 appears to be an older kernel version without xsk_skb_metadata at all. Note the desc copy: `*desc = ring->desc[idx];` — a struct copy into local desc, then validation on the copy, and the copy is what's used downstream. That's actually a single-fetch (a struct assignment reads shared memory once into local). Though a struct copy is technically not atomic, the same local copy is validated and used — that satisfies the validated-equals-used invariant (each field within the copy is fixed at copy time). Actually wait — a struct assignment compiles to multiple loads, but each field is loaded once into the local. So validated value == used value. That matches the upstream design.

However, `xskq_cons_read_desc_batch` copies into pool->tx_descs, same pattern.

So in this snapshot, net/xdp has no TX metadata support. The intent says: search within net/xdp AND AF_XDP-capable driver TX-completion and metadata paths for UMEM-resident fields (xsk descriptor addr/len/options, tx_metadata request fields, flags) fetched more than once.

So I should check the drivers that implement AF_XDP TX (xsk_tx_metadata or zero-copy TX paths). Since s04 has no xsk_tx_metadata support in core, drivers likely don't have AF_XDP metadata either. But drivers do consume xsk descriptors via xsk_tx_peek_desc / xp_raw_get_data etc. Let me check the driver paths in s04.

Let me search drivers for xsk usage: drivers that call xsk_tx_peek_desc, xsk_buff_raw_get_data, xp_assign_dev, etc. The key: driver reads desc from the batch (already validated by xskq_cons_is_valid_desc against pool->addrs_cnt etc.) and then uses desc.addr/desc.len to access UMEM. Since the desc copy is local, validated value == used value. But maybe some driver re-reads from shared memory? Unlikely.

The real variant class here: any place where the UMEM content (packet data itself, which is userspace-writable) is read for validation then used. E.g., in the seed era, the metadata resided in the UMEM buffer. Without metadata support, the packet data itself is userspace-writable, but the kernel typically just DMAs or copies it — the data isn't used for control decisions, except... XDP_TX? Hmm.

Let me check the kernel version of s04 to know what's present.
